Retain the bounded retrieval-practice evidence while rewriting the reviewed protocol in Brali's explanatory voice. The page now teaches the difference between familiarity, retrieval, and application; removes inherited unsupported precision; and uses dry humor only to challenge learning theatre, not the reader. A 2021 systematic review supports retrieval practice for classroom learning/retention; two 2026 sources narrow interpretation by distinguishing direct and forward testing effects and showing that improved rule retention did not automatically produce better rule application in one classroom study.

Replace a rigid, unsupported after-lunch/1 p.m. rule and inherited dosing advice with a bounded protocol based on a fully reviewed 2025 randomized crossover trial. The trial directly tests caffeine dose and timing relative to bedtime. It supports a stronger caution around a single 400 mg dose and shows why dose matters, while its small all-male sample and acute capsule design do not justify universal personal cutoffs or claims that 100 mg four hours before bed is harmless for everyone.

Replace an inherited apology-and-forgiveness routine containing invented sincerity percentages, arbitrary timers and targets, and an implicit expectation that the harmed person should forgive. Experimental evidence supports apology as a causal signal that can promote forgiveness, and a large meta-analysis identifies apology and empathy as important correlates of forgiveness. The public protocol therefore focuses on accountable repair while preserving the other person's right not to forgive, reconcile, or continue the relationship.

Update the reviewed short-HIIT page with 2026 exercise-snack evidence. The strongest fresh synthesis is an RCT-only systematic review/meta-analysis of 21 studies (921 adults) showing moderate-certainty improvements in VO2max and peak power, while body-composition and blood-lipid findings remain low-certainty or inconclusive. A 2026 real-world randomized trial in 69 insufficiently active adults with type 2 diabetes provides an important boundary: four 1-minute vigorous bouts on at least five days per week were feasible, but did not outperform an active mobility/stretching comparator on most secondary cardiometabolic or fitness outcomes. The page therefore distinguishes a short interval session from exercise snacks spread through the day, keeps safety boundaries, and rejects one magic timer or cadence as an optimized prescription.

Replace inherited generic mind-wandering and treatment-like claims with a narrow auditory attention-flexibility drill that matches core Attention Training Technique operations described in systematic-review literature: externally focused selective attention, deliberate switching, and divided attention. Preserve uncertainty about clinical effects and do not present the simplified drill as Metacognitive Therapy or a treatment.

Refresh the existing reviewed progressive muscle relaxation protocol with a 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials focused on subjective sleep quality. The new synthesis supports PMR as a plausible low-cost sleep-support practice in the studied clinical populations, but high heterogeneity, possible publication bias, subjective outcomes, heterogeneous protocols and the absence of healthy-general-population trials in the review make a universal sleep claim inappropriate. The public protocol therefore keeps the conservative NHS technique, adds a sleep-specific use case and observation loop, and explicitly rejects magic session counts, mechanistic certainty and the claim that older adults do not benefit.

Replace an inherited sensory-mindfulness article containing unsupported adherence claims, fixed weekly dose targets, invented internal observations and treatment-like expectations with a conservative present-moment awareness protocol grounded in current NHS mindfulness guidance. The public version presents sensory noticing as a mindfulness exercise that may help someone reconnect with the present moment, not as a guaranteed treatment or a precise three-to-five-minute dose.

Keep the conservative short breath-meditation protocol while replacing brochure-like copy with Brali's teaching voice. NHS guidance supports a simple beginner practice with no universal session length and warns that mindfulness is not helpful for everyone. A 2026 preregistered network meta-analysis of 183 RCTs and 22,811 adults without diagnosed conditions adds a useful boundary: mindfulness is one evidence-informed route to general well-being alongside exercise, yoga, compassion and positive-psychology approaches, with no clear reason to present one as the universal winner. The page therefore teaches the attention-return loop, treats five minutes as a convenience rather than a dose, and normalizes switching practices when the method is unhelpful.

Replace an inherited pseudo-experiment with a conservative sleep-opportunity protocol. A 2021 systematic review/meta-analysis found that behavioral sleep-extension interventions increase sleep duration on average but with very high heterogeneity. AASM/SRS consensus recommends that healthy adults sleep seven or more hours per night on a regular basis. Neither source validates a 21-day optimization protocol, fixed wake-time tolerances, consumer sleep-stage targets, or an individual 'best' duration discovered from a small self-experiment.

Replace an inherited AI-coach article containing an invented universal schedule, neuroscience explanations, adherence tracking, app promotion and unsupported transfer claims with a source-bounded distributed-practice protocol for verbal recall.

Strengthen the existing conservative stress-walk protocol with a full-source-reviewed 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized and crossover-randomized trials of green exercise. The new evidence supports treating a safe green route as an optional modifier for short-term wellbeing and affect, while preserving the existing boundaries: ten minutes is not an evidence-defined dose, a forest is not required, effects are not guaranteed, and the review does not establish a unique biological mechanism or long-term treatment effect.

Replace an inherited Tabata article containing unsupported heart-rate formulas, calorie estimates, rep targets, injury claims, generic maximal-effort instructions and progression schedules with a conservative interval-timer protocol grounded in NHS physical-activity guidance and the original Tabata study. The public version explains that 20/10 x 8 is a historically specific high-intensity format, not a universal four-minute workout prescription.

Replace an inherited fear-disclosure article containing unsupported relief percentages, arbitrary word counts and timers, invented social-risk estimates and pseudo-clinical outcome expectations with a simple support-seeking protocol grounded in current NHS guidance. The public version focuses on choosing a trusted person, saying what is happening in plain language, asking for the kind of support wanted, respecting boundaries and seeking professional support when fear or anxiety significantly affects daily life.

Keep the conservative post-learning wakeful-rest protocol grounded in a 2026 meta-analysis of 142 effect sizes from 51 experimental studies, while adding a 2026 randomized classroom challenge study of 161 university students. The newer study found no consistent wakeful-rest advantage for factual recall or conceptual understanding of a complex expository text, so the public protocol is explicitly restricted to an optional declarative-memory experiment and must not claim better comprehension or general learning performance.

Replace an inherited walking-meeting article containing unsupported cognition percentages, step and heart-rate estimates, wind and battery pseudo-precision, and overbroad cardiometabolic claims. Two full-text 2026 systematic reviews/meta-analyses support a narrower claim: in acute controlled settings, interrupting prolonged sitting with physical activity, especially walking or light-to-moderate movement, improves postprandial glucose and insulin outcomes. The evidence does not test walking meetings as a format, establish a universal timer, or show long-term disease prevention.
